image.shortdescription: A square divided into three regions in the plane.

description.p: A square with vertices O (the origin), A at the point (1,0), B at the point (1,1), and C at the point (0,1). The square is divided into three regions. Region \mathcal{R}_1 is the bottom-right corner of the square, bounded above by the curve y=x^3 and below by the x-axis and to the right by the side of the square AB. Region \mathcal{R}_2 is the upper-left corner of the square, bounded below by y=\sqrt{x}, and to the left by the y-axis and above by the top line CB of the square. Region \mathcal{R}_3 is the remainder of the square not included in the other two regions, bounded above by y=\sqrt{x} and bounded below by y=x^3.

statement.p: Referring to the figure above, find the volume generated by rotating the region \mathcal{R}_2 about the line OA.
